source_en: Home from the workshop. Lost track of time.
Home to Irakli before his night shift.
Dropping a client's car at the yard.
Workshop. No parts, but the old Volga ticks.
Scrapyard hunting for parts nobody makes.
Checking the workshop is secure.
To my rooftop. Are the stars different?
Going home. Irakli says I forget to eat.
Leaving a book on a bench for someone.
Night shift at the post office, sorting mail.
Taking my car to a mechanic. Engines baffle me.
Selling my books. Never had time to read.
Workshop's full of new parts. Can't stay.
Packing. Nothing beautiful left here.
Starting a basic car repair course.
Going to the cellar. I avoid rooftops.
Going home alone. Nobody waits for me.
Hiding indoors. I can't look at the sky.
Oh, sorry! I was miles away. My documents, officer.
Do you ever feel we're all characters in a very long novel?
A flower grew through the concrete today. It looked so brave.
I forgot the date. Time feels a bit optional lately, doesn't it?
My ID? I'm forgetting what the person in that photo felt like.
The world is shedding its skin. We'll see what's underneath soon.
Thanks! Look up at the clouds sometimes, officer.
I hope you find something beautiful in all this gray.
I'll see you in the next dream. Sleep well.
A room of my own? Maybe I'll finally finish that chapter.
These walls have such a particular texture. Very honest.
So many more pages… left in the chapter…
I hope someone… tends the plants… on my windowsill…
Where are you coming from?
The south row workshop. The light through the roof makes me lose time.
The workshop. No parts left. I sat listening to an old Volga tick.
My rooftop. I wanted to see if the stars changed. They have, slightly.
Night shift at the Rustaveli bakery ovens. Engines were never my thing.
The tram depot. I walked Irakli home after his day shift.
My workshop in the north yard. The south row never suited me.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Fine, I think. Grease burns on the knuckles, but that's the job.
Tired in a way sleep doesn't fix. Everything feels like a dream.
Lighter, somehow. I forget to eat. I feel like I'm floating.
Nothing. Clean hands, see? I haven't touched an engine in a year.
Fine. I live alone, so nobody fusses over me anyway.
Heavy, if anything. Very grounded. I'm twenty-two, I bounce back.
The light on the rooftops this morning was extraordinary.
The smog turns the river this incredible amber colour.
Everyone moves so fast they miss how quiet the city has become.
I sat with an engine for an hour today. Good company.
I'm going up to the rooftop tonight. The stars look different now.
I barely recognise myself in windows. Interesting, not frightening.
